customManagers.description: The Go analyzers the check runner shells out to are pinned as `@vX.Y.Z` string literals inside `EnsureGoTool(...)` calls, so no manager sees them. They went stale silently until a Go 1.27 bump broke CI: staticcheck 2026.1 can't decode Go 1.27 export data, and the toolchain PR had no way to know the pin needed to move with it. `packageName` captures the module root (`honnef.co/go/tools`) because the goproxy 404s on a package path (`honnef.co/go/tools/cmd/staticcheck`), while `depName` keeps the full install path so `autoReplaceStringTemplate` can write the line back verbatim. The first argument is skipped as `[^,]+` because every call passes `ctx.RootDir` there; a pattern expecting a quoted string matched nothing.

The browser build's LLVM clang (compiles SQLite for wasm32) is pinned as `conda:<tool>@<version>` constants in the wasm build script, each under a `// renovate: datasource=conda depName=conda-forge/<tool>` comment, and installed into a private mise home, never `.mise.toml` (the conda env ships its own `cc`/`ar`/`ld`; `scripts/build-listing-wasm/toolchain.go` says why). No manager reads Go constants, so this one does.

packageRules.description: The wasm toolchain's clang and llvm-tools move together: `TestBothToolsArePinnedToOneLLVMRelease` fails a PR that bumps only one.

The check runner's Go analyzers land on their own, for the same reason the linters below do: an analyzer bump re-flags tracked source across every Go module, which is noise to review mixed in with dependency changes. `go.uber.org/nilaway` publishes no tags, so its pseudo-version pin gets no PRs; move it by hand when it matters.

Default lane for non-major updates. Split per app below, because one repo-wide batch pooled five unrelated breakages (a genai field, a new stylelint rule, an oxfmt reformat, two typecheck breaks) into a single 2,300-line PR that couldn't be reviewed or bisected. Per-app groups stay small enough to fix in one sitting.

Desktop app deps, Rust and JS together (a specta bump regenerates bindings.ts, so they have to land as one). Dashboard-only, because a desktop PR can never go green on its own: every lockfile touch leaves `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` stale, and the check only REGENERATES on a local run (`docs/guides/update-dependencies.md`). Renovate can't run that regeneration, since `postUpgradeTasks` needs a self-hosted `allowedCommands`. On top of that, semver-minor Rust crates break compilation for real (russh 0.63 changed the `check_server_key` signature and broke `cmdr-sftp`), which no bot fixes. Both attempted PRs failed: #41 closed, #97 red for five days. So Renovate keeps discovering versions and lists them on the Dependency Dashboard; a human ticks the box, or the weekly `/weekly-upgrades` pass does the whole batch in a worktree.
Worker + dashboard deps: both are Cloudflare-targeted and share wrangler.

Linters and formatters land on their own: a version bump here rewrites or re-flags tracked files across every app, which is noise to review mixed in with real dependency changes. The group touches `apps/desktop/package.json`, so the desktop rule above would make it dashboard-only (a later rule overrides only the fields it sets), and it sat in Pending Approval from 2026-09-14 on. Linters never reach the third-party notices, so their PR can go green: approval off, automerge back on.

Docker images, pinned by digest for Scorecard's Pinned-Dependencies (`FROM image:tag@sha256:...`), so a tag that upstream re-points can't change what we build. Every digest refresh and non-major tag bump across all Dockerfiles and compose files lands as one weekly PR that automerges on green CI, overriding the per-app groups above (the desktop one would otherwise hold the test-fixture images for dashboard approval). Majors still go through the dashboard rule below. The top-level `dockerfile` / `docker-compose` blocks give these two managers their own `ignorePaths`, without `**/test/**`, since most images are test fixtures. The listmonk image's tag is an ARG, which Renovate can't read: `infra/listmonk/README.md` § Updates.

The E2E base image's `rust` stage moves with `rust-toolchain.toml`, never on its own: the `e2e-rust-image-pin` check fails when the image tag or the `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN` env next to it differs from the pinned channel. A bump here alone would turn that check red on the whole automerged `docker images` group, and the toolchain pin moves through the dashboard-approved desktop group. So whoever bumps the pin bumps this too, guided by the check. Skipping the digest refreshes costs nothing, since `Dockerfile.base` copies only the toolchain dirs out of this image, never its Debian layer.

The SMB fixture containers are vendored from smb2's consumer test harness (`apps/desktop/test/smb-servers/.compose/VENDORED.md`), so their tags follow smb2: a bump here would drift from the source and fight the next re-vendor. Only the digest refreshes stay, since the digest pins are ours (a re-vendor keeps them) and they're what keeps the pinned base images patched.
The fixture compose files name their locally built images (`cmdr-sftp-fixture:latest` and friends); no registry has them.

Majors, dashboard-only for the same reason as the desktop group: a major needs code changes, so an unattended PR just sits red and mails about it (#61, TypeScript v7, sat red for ten days). Renovate still tracks what's available; `/weekly-upgrades` decides which ones to take.
schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

packageRules.description: Security patches get immediate PRs, auto-merge

First-party crates (David's own). Stricter pre-release gate than the 3-day window protects against, so no age gate. In Cmdr they still wait for dashboard approval (the desktop rule's, since this rule doesn't override it): a bump renames the version in the committed third-party notices, which a bot PR can't regenerate. The weekly pass takes them.

The specta trio stays on rc.24 / 0.0.11. rc.25 types every plain `f32`/`f64` as `number | null`. On return values that's defensible (serde_json renders NaN/Infinity as null), but it does the same to PARAMETERS, where it's wrong: `viewer_get_lines(target_value: f64)` and the four `media_index_*_threshold` commands take non-Option floats and serde rejects a JSON null for them. Adopting it trades a latent, never-observed hazard for a live one, plus ~25 sites of null-handling. Rationale: `apps/desktop/src-tauri/DETAILS.md` § Number types over IPC. Re-evaluate on the next rc; bump all three together or not at all.

The CVE overrides in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` are each scoped to one major (`js-yaml@3: ^3.15.2`) so every parent keeps its own line; a major bump of a value (`^4`) would drag the old-major parents onto an API they don't speak, which is what the scoping exists to prevent. Patches and minors to them still flow. Drop an override by hand once `pnpm why` shows its parents past the fix (the file's own comment).
The SMB benchmark harness pins sspi and smb-rpc in lockstep with smb 0.11's internal pins; independent bumps can never resolve, so leave the whole harness alone.
